subject: dermatology
title: Genodermatoses: Key High-Yield Lessons for NEET-PG

steps.tx: Genodermatoses are inherited skin disorders, and several are favourite exam topics. **Tuberous sclerosis** is autosomal dominant and follows Vogt's triad of epilepsy, intellectual disability and facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum). Skin clues include ash-leaf macules, shagreen patches and Koenen's periungual fibromas.
steps.say: Genodermatoses are inherited skin disorders, and several are favourite exam topics. Tuberous sclerosis is autosomal dominant and follows Vogt's triad of epilepsy, intellectual disability and facial angiofibromas, also called adenoma sebaceum. Skin clues include ash-leaf macules, shagreen patches and Koenen's periungual fibromas.

steps.tx: **Neurofibromatosis type 1** is autosomal dominant and caused by NF1 on chromosome 17. **Axillary freckling** (Crowe sign) is a pathognomonic sign. Six or more café-au-lait spots, two or more neurofibromas and two or more Lisch nodules are diagnostic criteria. NF2 instead causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas.
steps.say: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is autosomal dominant and caused by a defect in the NF1 gene on chromosome 17. Axillary freckling, known as Crowe sign, is a pathognomonic sign. Six or more café-au-lait spots, two or more neurofibromas and two or more Lisch nodules are diagnostic criteria. Type 2 instead causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas.

steps.tx: **Incontinentia pigmenti** is X-linked dominant and is lethal in males in utero, so it affects females. Lesions follow Blaschko lines and pass through four stages: vesicular, verrucous, hyperpigmented and atrophic. **Epidermal nevus** is verrucous and shows perinuclear vacuolation in the spinous and granular layers. **Darier disease** is autosomal dominant and shows suprabasal acantholysis with dyskeratosis.
steps.say: Incontinentia pigmenti is X-linked dominant and is lethal in males in utero, so it mainly affects females. Lesions follow Blaschko lines and pass through four stages: vesicular, verrucous, hyperpigmented and atrophic. Verrucous epidermal nevus shows perinuclear vacuolation in the spinous and granular layers. Darier disease is autosomal dominant and shows suprabasal acantholysis with dyskeratosis.

steps.tx: **Ichthyosis vulgaris** is autosomal dominant with reduced filaggrin and an absent granular layer, causing crocodile or sauroderma scales that spare the flexures. **X-linked ichthyosis** is due to steroid sulfatase deficiency and is linked to cryptorchidism. **Harlequin ichthyosis** is autosomal recessive and is caused by ABCA12 mutations.

X-linked ichthyosis is due to steroid sulfatase deficiency and is linked to cryptorchidism. Harlequin ichthyosis is autosomal recessive and is caused by ABCA12 mutations.

steps.tx: **Epidermolysis bullosa** is a blistering group of genetic disorders. The dystrophic form, with defective anchoring fibrils, is caused by COL7A1 mutations that encode type 7 collagen. Congenital blistering after handling in an infant, with a fatal sibling, points to this inherited form. **Xeroderma pigmentosum** is a DNA repair defect that predisposes to skin cancer.

steps.tx: **Hailey-Hailey disease** is benign familial chronic pemphigus, an autosomal dominant condition with flexural erosions and suprabasal acantholysis. **Muir-Torre syndrome** shows multiple sebaceous tumours as a marker of internal malignancy. **Acrodermatitis enteropathica** is autosomal recessive with low zinc absorption and needs lifelong zinc supplementation.
